blocks.text: Tunneled dialysis catheter placement - right IJ, antegrade tunnel

items: Adult TDC, commonly 14.5 Fr; select length by measured course and device-specific tip-to-cuff length.
Micropuncture set: 21G needle, 0.018-inch wire, and 4-5 Fr introducer. Working wire: compatible 0.035-inch Bentson or kit-specified wire.
Matched dilators, peel-away sheath, and tunneler. Sheath size and valve vary by kit; do not choose by catheter French size alone.
Ultrasound with sterile cover, fluoroscopy, maximal sterile barriers, skin prep, lidocaine, and #11 blade.
Saline, 10 mL or larger syringes, lumen caps, prescribed lock solution, and dressing.
Absorbable neck-closure and nonabsorbable securement sutures; 3-0 Vicryl/Prolene are local options to confirm with the attending, not universal requirements.

confirm right IJ patency and carotid position with ultrasound. Mark venotomy and chest exit; roughly two fingerbreadths below the clavicle is a planning landmark, not a fixed rule. Adjust for catheter length, cuff position, and a smooth tunnel.
use maximal sterile barriers; allow skin prep to dry. Infiltrate the neck, exit site, and entire planned tunnel, tracking the total lidocaine dose.
make a controlled #11 skin nick sized for the introducer; bluntly free superficial tissue as needed. Keep the blade away from the wire, vein, and catheter; do not dissect blindly toward the vein.
puncture under real-time ultrasound with the 21G needle. Advance the 0.018-inch wire without resistance and confirm venous course before introducing the micropuncture sheath.

through the compatible introducer, advance the selected wire under fluoroscopy into the IVC. Confirm it has not entered the right ventricle; stop for resistance or ectopy. Retain wire and introducer during tunneling.
make an incision just large enough to pass the catheter cuff, rather than using blade widths as a fixed measurement. Confirm adequate tunnel length and room for the external hub.

flush and prepare the catheter per its instructions, then attach the tunneler securely. Pass subcutaneously from chest exit toward venotomy, tenting the skin near the neck exit. Avoid deep passage, sharp turns, and wire damage.
draw the catheter through without twisting or stretching it. Bury the cuff fully at the device-specified distance from the exit; confirm a gentle neck curve with no kink or hub buried in the wound.

remove the small introducer while holding the wire. Dilate over the confirmed central wire, then advance the matched sheath/dilator under fluoroscopy only as far as needed. Never force or blindly hub a rigid dilator.

know whether the sheath is valved before removing its dilator. Keep the system occluded during exchanges; a valve reduces but does not eliminate air-entry risk. Coordinate respiration/ventilation with anesthesia as appropriate.

advance through the sheath under fluoroscopy, using over-wire placement only if supported by the catheter/stylet system. Peel the sheath in a controlled fashion while holding catheter position. Remove all wires/stylets and confirm the device-specific dialysis tip position, usually mid right atrium, without wall contact or kinking.

aspirate for brisk blood return and flush each lumen easily with saline using a 10 mL or larger syringe. Keep hubs closed when disconnected. Poor return or resistance requires reassessment of tip position, twist, or kink; a three-second fill test is not a universal acceptance criterion.
obtain hemostasis and approximate the incision with the chosen absorbable closure. If using a buried interrupted stitch, invert the knot and avoid capturing or compressing the catheter.

anchor to skin using the designated suture wings/device. If an attending uses crossed securement ties, follow the device instructions; never puncture, strangulate, or narrow the catheter. Knot/throw counts depend on material and technique, not a fixed 4/4/4/7 sequence.

lock each lumen with the prescribed solution and labeled fill volume, clamp/cap per device instructions, and apply a sterile dressing. Save final fluoroscopy and document tip position, function, lock volumes, and readiness for dialysis.
confirm vein and wire before dilation; large-bore arterial cannulation needs specialist assessment before removal.
occlude open hubs and sheaths; minimize open-system time.
new ectopy warrants repositioning; avoid contact with the atrial wall or tricuspid valve.
check tip depth, kinks, thrombus, and fibrin sheath; do not force flushing or advancement.
suspected bloodstream or tunnel infection requires a specific removal/exchange and antibiotic plan, not an automatic wire exchange.
maintain wire control and release the cuff without cutting the catheter; stop traction if centrally adherent.
